title: Word Break
summary: Determine if a string can be divided into segments using words from a given dictionary, where words can be reused.
statement: Determine if a string can be divided into segments using words from a given dictionary, where words can be reused.
constraints: s has 1–300 lowercase letters. The dictionary contains 1–1000 distinct nonempty lowercase words, each at most 20 letters long.
Use one or more dictionary words to cover all of s in order. Words may be reused; return only whether a complete segmentation exists.
hints: A successful first word does not guarantee that the remaining suffix can be segmented.
Record which prefix lengths are reachable by complete dictionary words.
Start with prefix length zero reachable. Mark end reachable if an earlier reachable start has s[start:end] in the dictionary; return reachability at len(s).
Limit candidate word lengths by the longest dictionary word. Reusing a word requires no removal from the dictionary.
editorial: A prefix of length end is segmentable exactly when some earlier segmentable prefix is followed by a dictionary word. Fill these reachability states left-to-right, considering only starts within the maximum dictionary-word length L. Set membership handles dictionary lookup; Python slicing and hashing make the conservative bound O(nL²), plus dictionary construction. The independent oracle enumerates all subsets of the string's gaps as potential cut positions on small inputs. The 300-character stress cases use directly established answers.

tests.explanation: The complete split leet|code uses dictionary words, so return True.
Split apple|pen|apple. Reusing apple is permitted.
